system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status note:** No written authority from Amelia Frost has been received for any fallback position. All recommendations below are at playbook starting positions unless stated.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is our conditional fallback only, and no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation: REJECT all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13), plus a proposal that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the default-application language is a back-door override of the fundamental/fraud carve-outs.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT outright.** Collapsing title into the general regime would cap our recovery for non-ownership of the shares at 20% and 18 months – commercially unacceptable for a 100% acquisition.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). No fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insert express carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and 12 generally.** This is non-negotiable under the playbook and no one on the buyer side has authority to waive it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: REJECT [1.1] and [1.2] of the Disclosure Letter and Sch 7 general disclosure; require each disclosure to be specific and fairly made with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter.** Blanket data-room disclosure would effectively neutralise the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion of blanket exclusion. Any residual qualifier must reference named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: DELETE cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" (constructive) knowledge combined with whole-data-room disclosure would bar virtually every claim; if any qualifier survives it must be actual-knowledge, buyer-side named individuals, and carved out for title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL [2] confirms no final written consent and no evidence conditions under cl 11.3 are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent obtained AND evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a Condition Precedent to Completion; not consent-on-delivery; endeavours obligation stronger than "reasonable."
- **Recommendation: REJECT; redraft as a hard CP requiring unconditional effective consent plus documentary evidence of condition satisfaction, with a best/all reasonable endeavours covenant.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) and the Seller itself admits nothing is in hand.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL [3] confirms not repaid and no discharge in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT post-completion release; require payout figure, funds-flow line to Riverlark, and executed releases/PPSR discharges at Completion.** Debt-free/cash-free pricing is defeated if AUD 3.2m of secured debt and its security survive Completion; any post-completion mechanism requires an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval (none given).

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL [5] confirms they are absent and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item (deducted from price) or expressly seller-funded with a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the silent exclusion; require itemisation of bonuses and all on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) in the funds flow or a dollar-for-dollar Seller indemnity.** Completion-triggered bonuses are a Seller-caused, Completion-crystallised liability that would otherwise land in the acquired company's P&L.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4] confirms cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010 (unverified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering non-transfer, defective title and third-party claims regarding Ironquay-developed IP, with the SOW3 cure (payment + confirmatory assignment) preserved as the primary remedy.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "adequate"; broaden cl 11.1 to cover all loss from Ironquay IP ownership/transfer defects, require pre-Completion payment and confirmatory assignment of Project Materials, and treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified pending bank evidence.** A payment-only indemnity does not deliver the IP itself if the assignment condition is never satisfied.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** DD-006 is a "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL [6]: ~1,240 records, unintended external recipient, access/scope/notification duty unestablished, no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, completed investigation, interim updates, and a specific indemnity or warranty for the incident; no assumption either way on breach, harm or notification.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; require a pre-Completion covenant to preserve logs, complete the investigation with regular written updates, and a specific indemnity for any loss arising.** The Seller's own disclosure concedes the facts are undetermined, so materiality cannot be assessed and no numeric position should be taken in either direction.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL [8] does not confirm whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Factual assessment (timing, term, termination rights, accrual status) before any classification.
- **Recommendation: NEITHER accept the Seller's characterisation nor claim an automatic Debt/price deduction; request DD-008/DD-011 read together with termination and accrual detail, then decide.** The playbook prohibits a reflexive Debt classification and the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/covenant and specific indemnity categories kept separate with their own caps and time limits; no default general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: REJECT all three override mechanisms (cl 12.3/13 default, cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims," and the Tax/IP sweep); insert an express priority clause that general limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims.** The Seller's drafting achieves through three separate clauses what it could not achieve openly in SPA-N-004.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL [10] concedes this is the "source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances (PPSR, Riverlark security), authority and capacity.
- **Recommendation: Do not treat DD-012 as proof; commission ASIC company search, PPSR search, review of the constitution and board/shareholder authorisations, and obtain Seller board minutes and a title warranty under the fundamental regime.** A register maintained by the Seller-controlled company is a supplied internal document, not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled" under the general 20%/18-month regime.
- **Buyer wants:** These remain open; separate Tax indemnity and IP warranty regime to be negotiated; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "settled"; record in the issues list that Tax and IP terms are OPEN and reserved, and that nothing in this round constitutes agreement.** The Seller cannot unilaterally close a category that was never negotiated, and the playbook requires we hold it open without overreaching to unlimited liability.

---

**Summary of escalations required:** None of the Seller's positions trigger an available fallback; SPA-N-001 (20% cap) and SPA-N-003 (18 months) would require Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft before any movement. SPA-N-005 (fraud carve-out) cannot be waived by anyone. SPA-N-009 would require both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval if any post-completion mechanism is contemplated.
=== END ADVICE ===
